html:
The Seneca, who call themselves Onöndowa'ga:', "people of the great hill", are the westernmost nation of the Haudenosaunee (Iroquois) Confederacy. Their homeland lies between the Finger Lakes and the Genesee River in what is now western New York.

As the largest nation of the league they were the "keepers of the western door". In the 1650s they led wars that destroyed or absorbed the Huron, the Neutral and the Erie. In the American Revolution most Seneca fought for Britain; in 1779 the Sullivan Expedition burned their towns and fields.

After the war their leaders, such as Cornplanter and Red Jacket, bargained for what land they could, and the Treaty of Canandaigua of 1794 confirmed some of it. In 1799 the Seneca prophet Handsome Lake began the Longhouse religion, which many Haudenosaunee still follow. In the 1960s the Kinzua Dam flooded much of the Allegany reservation, despite their treaty. See also Iroquois.
